headline.text: Google says free Gemini users lose its Flash and Pro models on Oct. 9

slides.altText: Google says free Gemini users lose its Flash and Pro models on Oct. 9

headline.text: Free Gemini drops to one model

slides.altText: Free Gemini drops to one model

body.text: Google says free users will lose Flash and Pro on Oct. 9 and be limited to Flash-Lite, which its support page describes as built for speed and everyday tasks like summarization and brainstorming.

headline.text: Paying $4.99 no longer gets you Pro

slides.altText: Paying $4.99 no longer gets you Pro

body.text: Google says AI Plus subscribers keep Flash-Lite and Flash but lose Pro, its most advanced model. Google says it will email them the date, which may differ from Oct. 9.

headline.text: Keeping Pro means a bigger bill

slides.altText: Keeping Pro means a bigger bill

body.text: Pro will require AI Pro or AI Ultra. Yahoo Creators calculates a Plus subscriber would pay roughly $15 more a month, or $180 a year, to keep it, at current prices.

slides.secondNote: Google AI Pro US monthly price

headline.text: Eligible U.S. students get a free Pro year

slides.altText: Eligible U.S. students get a free Pro year

body.text: Yahoo Creators says eligible U.S. college students can get a year of AI Pro free, redeemable through Dec. 31, 2026. It needs a valid payment method and charges $19.99 a month afterward unless canceled.

headline.text: Higher effort uses more of your limit

slides.altText: Higher effort uses more of your limit: "…provide more thorough answers to queries, but will also use more of your limit." (Google (support page))

body.text: Google’s support page says it is adding low, medium and high effort levels for each available model.

quoteText.text: …provide more thorough answers to queries, but will also use more of your limit.

headline.text: PCMag counts a second plan overhaul this year

slides.altText: PCMag counts a second plan overhaul this year

body.text: 9to5Google says the limits follow a May move to compute-based usage limits, which weigh prompt complexity and chat length. PCMag suggests rising storage and component costs may play a part. Google gave no reason.

caption:
Google says that starting Oct. 9, 2026, Gemini app users without a paid Google AI plan will be limited to the Flash-Lite model and will lose Flash and Pro.

Google AI Plus subscribers ($4.99 a month) will also lose Pro, on a date Google says it will announce by email. Pro will require AI Pro ($19.99 a month) or AI Ultra. The details come from an updated Google support page, as reported by 9to5Google, PCMag and Engadget. Google has given no reason for the change. PCMag suggests rising storage and component costs may play a part, and notes this is the second overhaul of Google’s AI plans this year.

Flash-Lite is the lightest model, built for everyday tasks like summarizing and brainstorming. Pro is Google’s most advanced model, for complex math and coding.
